prize_parts.citation: for the collateral-based theory of credit cycles and macroeconomic amplification

statement.case_for: B037 remains the strongest prize-ready achievement on maturity, conceptual influence, and exact attribution. Kiyotaki and Moore supplied the distinctive mechanism linking collateral values, borrowing capacity, asset prices, and aggregate fluctuations. The mechanism has become foundational in macro-finance and has generated sustained theoretical and quantitative work. The narrower two-person formulation identifies one coherent discovery without making empirical claims beyond what the mechanism can establish.
statement.case_against: Even a narrowly framed collateral mechanism is difficult to isolate empirically from other financial frictions, and its quantitative importance depends on model structure and institutional setting. The broader ballot description also includes the financial accelerator, an important related contribution that cannot be represented fully by a Kiyotaki-Moore-only award.

responses.point: Krusell argues that Kiyotaki and Moore are the central originators of the collateral-credit-cycle mechanism and that adding Gertler would join related but distinct formulations.
responses.response: I agree, and have changed my configuration accordingly. My round-one three-person formulation placed too much weight on the shared macro-financial insight relative to the requirement that a prize identify a bounded discovery. A Kiyotaki-Moore citation focused on collateral-based amplification is scientifically stronger and attributionally cleaner.

responses.point: Friberg argues that Marc Melitz is the identifiable originator of the canonical heterogeneous-firm trade framework and favors a narrow allocation over crediting later extensions as equivalent to the defining breakthrough.
responses.response: I find this attribution principle persuasive and applicable to B037. Mark Gertler's financial-accelerator work is major, but it should not be folded into the distinctive Kiyotaki-Moore collateral mechanism merely to form a broader trio. B044 consequently remains a leading alternative, particularly if its citation is centered on Melitz's defining innovation.

responses.point: Hassler emphasizes that B049 gains strength from a compact foundational pair and a citation confined to its core welfare-theoretic contribution.
responses.response: I agree with the general standard of compact attribution and limited citation scope. It favors a Kiyotaki-Moore award over my prior broader B037 package, while B037 retains an advantage in the unusually clear transmission mechanism connecting credit conditions to macroeconomic amplification.

uncertainties: Whether a citation centered on collateral-based amplification can be kept sufficiently distinct from the broader financial-accelerator literature.
How far available empirical evidence can separately identify collateral amplification from other financial frictions.
Whether the committee should instead recognize the equally mature but more individually attributable heterogeneous-firm trade framework in B044.
statement.conflict_note: No candidate-specific conflict is apparent from the supplied profile. My documented coauthors do not include either proposed laureate.
